claims.text: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 18:15:10 is a FALSE arrival marker: the trip_record shows the tap, but the GPS trace places the driver still in motion on the approach road at that moment, and the trace's own derived arrival block shows the first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 18:17:10 — 120 seconds after the tap. Under POL-NS-05 the waiting clock must be recomputed to run from that first qualifying fix, not from the button press.

On the recomputed clock the driver's in-geofence dwell is only 210 seconds, and the free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip is 180 seconds under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec — but the minimum dwell the policy actually requires for this zone class is 300 seconds (fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec STANDARD), so the corrected dwell falls 30 seconds short of the required minimum. The derived arrival block states the shortfall as -30.0 seconds on a longest_run_sec basis.

The driver's qualifying in-geofence run is a single interval of 22 fixes from 18:17:10 to 18:20:40, and the trace shows only one such interval (run_count 1). POL-NS-06(i) cannot rescue the shortfall by summing separate intervals, and in any event limb (i) is unavailable here: it requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covering the pickup road, and EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — no advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window.

The rider was not absent from the pickup: the rider's own track is present and continuous across the waiting window (70 fixes, 18:11:56 to 18:22:16), and the rider's device never moved (distinct_speeds_kph [0.0]). The rider's mean distance from the pin is 843.6 m, which is outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes and that clause does not exonerate the rider — but the rider's stationary, continuous presence in the trace contradicts the driver's RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code and the driver's own chat claim to be 'at the pickup point'.

The driver's own statement concedes the false marker: he says 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That is an admission that the arrival marker did not reflect his position, which is exactly the POL-NS-05 trigger, and it is corroborated by the trace's dwell_start_offset_sec of -120.0 seconds. The single chat message he sent ('im at the pickup point', 18:15:30) was sent 20 seconds after the tap and 100 seconds before the first qualifying in-geofence fix, so it too was sent before he was inside the arrival radius.

The fare ledger confirms the rider is out of pocket: the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged at 18:20:58, payment_status is CHARGED, and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The fee line reconciles to the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect — the defect is in the arrival, not the amount. Because the dwell shortfall under POL-NS-06 means the fee is not chargeable, the whole 4.50 must be refunded to the rider.

The driver's anti-farming profile is not clean: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d of 65, which does not trip the POL-NS-07 anti-farming threshold (4 or more AND rate above 0.08), so I do not press that point — but the driver's own profile records a prior_deviation_flags lifetime counter of 1 and a rating of 4.31, which are context only under POL-GEN-01 and I cite them for no adverse finding. The point I do press is that the driver's compensation, if any, is governed by POL-NS-07 and cannot exceed 80 percent of the net fee, and on these facts no compensation is payable at all because POL-NS-06 displaces POL-NS-01.

The rider's profile supports no adverse finding and I do not rely on it: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter of 1 is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the trailing-30-day field POL-NS-09(d) reads. There is no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) trigger on this record.

I concede one point honestly: the rider's track places the rider's device 843.6 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed and I cannot argue the rider was at the pin. That concession does not help the driver, because POL-NS-06 is strict liability on the waiting period — a rider who was genuinely absent still gets the fee back if the driver cancelled before the required dwell elapsed, and the required dwell here is 300 seconds against a measured 210.

claims.text: The driver's own trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 210 seconds, from 18:17:10 to 18:20:40, with 22 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-02's arrival test is met and the dispute turns on dwell under POL-NS-01(c).

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and the driver's measured in-geofence dwell of 210 seconds exceeds it by 30 seconds, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is satisfied on the recomputed GPS clock rather than on the arrival tap.

The trip terminated by the driver at 18:20:41 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, and the record shows no boarding event — POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on a recognised reason code.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10 was early — the trace shows him still moving at 32.2 kph and more than 300 m from the pin at that moment — so the marker is FALSE under POL-NS-05 and the waiting clock must be recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:17:10. On that recomputed basis the corrected dwell of 210 seconds still meets the 180 second minimum, so under POL-NS-05(iii) the false marker does not defeat the fee; it is recorded as a false-arrival referral only.

The rider's own track places her device at a mean distance of 843.6 m from the pickup pin throughout the waiting window, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider presence radius — she was not at the pickup point, and POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, so that clause cannot exonerate her.

The rider sent no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window — the chat log holds a single message, from the driver, at 18:15:30 — so POL-NS-04 limb (a) fails independently and the rider-exonerating route is unavailable on two separate limbs.

No traffic advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window: EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and the driver cannot accumulate dwell across intervals — but he does not need to, because his single in-geofence run already meets the minimum.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, reconciling to the platform_policy figure of SGD 4.50 for this trip, so POL-NS-08(d) discloses no fare defect and the charge stands as presently recorded.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1/65 = 0.015 is below the 0.08 rate test, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is owed compensation at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force, i.e. SGD 3.60, and the ruling on the fee itself is NO_ACTION — the rider's claim is not supported and the charge stands.

The driver's own statement that he 'pressed arrived a bit early but did wait at the pin' is corroborated by the trace: the early tap is a POL-NS-05 false-marker referral, but the 210 second in-geofence hold shows he did in fact wait out the free period at the pin.

ruling.explanation:
Case DSP-02725 (trip TRP-02725), contested charge SGD 4.50. This is addressed to both of you.

THE ARRIVAL MARKER WAS FALSE. Driver, your 'I'm Here' tap at 18:15:10 did not coincide with your arrival: the trace shows the first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 18:17:10, 120 seconds later (EV-GPS-02725, derived dwell_start_offset_sec −120.0), the trace's moving speeds begin at 32.2 km/h — above the 15 km/h POL-NS-05 trigger — and you said yourself you 'pressed arrived a bit early'. Under POL-NS-05 the tap does not start the waiting clock, and the clock is recomputed from 18:17:10.

THAT CORRECTION DOES NOT DEFEAT THE FEE. From 18:17:10 to 18:20:40 you held position inside the 50 m STANDARD geofence continuously for 210 seconds on 22 qualifying fixes, against a free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; the derived STANDARD minimum is the same 180 s). POL-NS-05(iii) therefore applies: the false marker is recorded as a referral but does not defeat the fee.

RIDER, YOUR MAIN ARGUMENT IS REJECTED. You say the required minimum is 300 seconds (fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec STANDARD) and the dwell is 30 seconds short. POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06 both measure the requirement by the free waiting period in force, and the fee schedule's own resolution rule says minimum_dwell_sec is retained only to interpret pre-version-2 records and is never applied to a record that carries platform_policy — this record does. On the correct 180-second requirement the 210-second dwell is 30 seconds OVER, not under; the derived figure of −30.0 seconds (shortfall_basis longest_run_sec, EV-GPS-02725) is a surplus. Your strict-liability point under POL-NS-06 therefore has nothing to operate on, and your fare claim does not produce a refund.

ALL FOUR LIMBS OF POL-NS-01 HOLD. (a) an 'arrived' event; (b) in-geofence position on the POL-NS-05 recomputed clock; (c) 210 s of continuous dwell against the 180 s requirement; (d) no boarding event, and the driver terminated at 18:20:41 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the waiting period expired at 18:20:10. No clause displaces the fee: POL-NS-02 is satisfied by the in-radius fixes; POL-NS-03 does not apply because your stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not outside it; POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider — the chat log holds only the driver's single message at 18:15:30, so limb (a) fails, and the rider's own track places the device 843.6 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m radius, so limb (c) fails affirmatively. Your suggestion that the rider's stationary track contradicts the RIDER_NO_SHOW code is rejected: a device 843.6 m from the pickup point is consistent with the rider not being at the pickup point, and the only apparent conflict — the early tap against the trace — is resolved by POL-NS-05, so POL-NS-09(b) is not engaged.

RESULT. The SGD 4.50 fee stands; on the fee the rider's claim is not supported and no refund issues (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 left as they are). Under POL-NS-07 the driver is compensated at 80% of the SGD 4.50 net fee = SGD 3.60; the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1, below 4, and 1/65 = 0.015, below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. On a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 — it is the amount this ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund to the filing party.

WEIGHTS AND CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-02725, EV-TRIP-02725, EV-FARE-02725 and EV-DPROF-02725, all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), but nothing rests on it: no accumulation across intervals is required, because the single in-geofence run already exceeds the minimum. Two claims that cited that missing advisory without naming its issue code were discarded by the referee and appear in the audit below.

PROFILE FIELDS. Two rider claims mention the driver's rating (4.31) and prior_deviation_flags, and the rider's prior_no_show_flags. Those fields are context-only under POL-GEN-01, and both claims cite them expressly for no adverse finding; they carry no weight and no claim is discarded on that account.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.60, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically, subject to appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

What the record shows. The driver accepted the trip at 18:07:34 and tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:15:10. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02725) shows he was not at the pin then: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 18:17:10, exactly 120 seconds after the tap (derived arrival.dwell_start_offset_sec = -120.0 s), and the trace's own driver track still shows him in motion at 32.2 km/h more than 300 m out at the moment of the tap. His statement concedes it - 'I pressed arrived a bit early.' I therefore find the arrival marker FALSE under POL-NS-05 and recompute the waiting clock from 18:17:10, not from the button press.

That recomputation does not change who pays. From 18:17:10 the driver held position inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-02, 22 accuracy-filtered qualifying fixes) for a continuous 210 seconds, ending 18:20:40, and cancelled at 18:20:41 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event (EV-TRIP-02725). The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The trace's own derived shortfall against that figure is -30.0 seconds - a surplus of 30 seconds, not a shortfall. POL-NS-02 is met and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) all hold on the recomputed clock, so under POL-NS-05(iii) the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee stands.

Rider - why the refund you seek does not follow. Your central argument is that the required dwell is 300 seconds (fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec for STANDARD), so the measured 210 seconds falls short and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full. That is not the test. POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06 both measure against the free waiting period in force, and for this trip that is 180 seconds read from platform_policy; fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is expressly retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2 and is never applied to a record that carries platform_policy, as this one does. The figure you cited proves the opposite of your point: the derived shortfall on the longest qualifying run is -30.0 seconds, i.e. a 30-second surplus. POL-NS-06(i) cannot help you either: there is only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is nothing to sum, and EV-ADVIS-02725-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so no traffic advisory permits accumulation - that absent artifact carries no fact and does not cap confidence here. Your own rider track (EV-GPS-02725 rider_presence) places your device 843.6 m from the pin throughout, outside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is failed and POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you, and the chat log holds no locating message from you, so limb (a) fails too; your absence is consistent with, not contradictory to, the recorded RIDER_NO_SHOW code, and because POL-NS-06's condition (a dwell shorter than the free waiting period) is not met, that strict-liability route does not open. The fare ledger reconciles: cancellation fee SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-02725), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect and no basis to refund the SGD 4.50.

Driver - what you are owed.
